what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A morning brief so no thread is lost
sections.para: I work on many threads and miss ones worth returning to. A daily brief from the Librarian would cover yesterday across every repository, outside pull requests, releases, runs and their costs, reviews and moved briefs, then threads to pick up, what is coming and three leverage suggestions. The sources mostly exist; it learns from what I act on.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Yesterday, the agents, threads and leverage
sections.para: Many threads lose some. A daily brief before I start covers yesterday, the agents' debrief and what is coming, with threads to pick up and at most three leverage suggestions. The Librarian writes it, reading everything and writing only its folder. Release files, the run ledger, the briefs map and reviews already exist. It learns, and every team needs one.

sections.label: Why I need it
sections.line: Tangents and leverage make threads slip
sections.para: I am in a productive, tangent-following mode, working where leverage is highest, so I miss threads that become worth returning to; today I could not remember which cloud session built something. A morning brief of what happened, what the agents did, what I left and what is coming keeps the pace without loss.

sections.label: What it reads
sections.line: Releases, the ledger, briefs, reviews, GitHub
sections.para: Most sources exist: a file per release, the accountant's ledger of scheduled runs with costs and refusals, the briefs map, the review status, GitHub across my organisations with outside contributions, and the cloud sessions. A calendar file and the wires cover what is coming. GitHub's events feed is too short and lagged, so it searches by date.

sections.label: What it writes
sections.line: Six sections, short enough for a phone
sections.para: Needs you; yesterday per repository and outside contributions; the agents' debrief with aim, result, cost and what is open; threads to pick up with reasons; coming up; and at most three places where my leverage is. It is the feed of debriefs the agents' article asked for, every morning.

sections.label: The Librarian
sections.line: Reads everything, writes only its folder
sections.para: The Librarian catalogues and keeps things in sync. The site already names it, for unmapped tags and the rule flag, do not fix. Its policy: read everything, write one brief and data file a day and a run-log line, never edit, send, contact, merge or close anything. It flags; others fix.

sections.label: A loop that learns
sections.para: rUv's Ruflo describes a four-step learning loop for agents' work. The Librarian applies it to my attention: each brief records what I acted on, opened, picked up or called noise, and the next weights its sections by that, kept as a readable, editable file of weights rather than a hidden model.

sections.label: Others are building this too
sections.line: Pulse and Google brief from what they see
sections.para: ChatGPT Pulse, previewed in September 2025, leaves morning cards; Google tested a daily email in December 2025. They build on what a company sees of you. This builds on what I have written down: my repositories, releases, ledger and briefs, recorded openly in files I own.

sections.label: Every team needs one
sections.line: Every team needs one, started small
sections.para: Teams scatter work across repositories, tickets, chats and runs and lose threads. A Librarian reading it all each morning keeps a team in sync without a meeting. It can start with one repository and the release notes and be retrofitted backwards, as bringing my past work back proposes for my history.

sections.label: The brief
sections.line: The build note and its order
sections.para: The build note lists sources and how to read each, the page's sections, the loop, the runner and the tests, and is on the briefs page. Start with this repository alone, then GitHub across organisations, then cloud sessions, then threads and leverage, then the loop.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Not built; suggestions, a design, public counts
sections.para: Nothing runs yet. Leverage suggestions stay suggestions. The loop is a design, and Ruflo's own figures are self-reported. GitHub counts come from update dates on public pages. Unattended runs get blocked, so the brief must say when a source could not be read.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: GitHub docs, Ruflo, prior art, site files
sections.para: From a voice memo on 18 October 2026 and research that day: GitHub's events, search, rate-limit and schedule documentation, the organisations' pages, Ruflo's README and intelligence plugin, coverage of ChatGPT Pulse and Google's daily brief, and this site's releases, ledger, briefs map, reviews and policies.
